What if one of the defining energy challenges of this decade isn’t heating, but cooling?

In 2021, more than half a million people died from heat exposure, an increase of more than 60% since the 1990s. Every warming scenario tells us this is only the beginning.

Cooling is often seen as a household need, but it is essential across the entire development value chain. It keeps hospitals functioning, food systems running, and businesses productive. As temperatures rise and AI, digital infrastructure, and data centres drive growing electricity demand, cooling is becoming one of the defining pressures on energy systems. I have increasingly come to see cooling not as a matter of comfort, but as critical infrastructure for human development.

In this video, I share three reflections:

🔥 Heat is a justice issue. More than 1 billion people are already at high risk because they lack access to adequate cooling, with the greatest needs concentrated across the Global South, regions that have contributed the least to historical emissions. As temperatures rise, heat is amplifying existing inequalities and increasing risks for the most vulnerable communities.

📊 Cooling is a development multiplier. Cooling protects vaccines and medicines, keeps hospitals functioning, reduces food loss, and enables children to learn in safe classrooms. Today, around 13% of food is lost between harvest and retail, much of it because of inadequate cold chains.

⚡ The future of cooling depends on sustainable energy. Without action, global cooling demand could more than triple by 2050. Yet a sustainable cooling practices could cut cooling-related emissions by 64% while expanding access.

There is reason for optimism. Between 2015 and 2022, the number of countries with national cooling policies increased from 21 to 176. But policies alone are not the finish line. The next challenge is implementation at the speed and scale that today’s climate reality demands.

In a warming world, achieving SDG 7 is no longer only about expanding access to energy. It is about ensuring that energy protects lives, strengthens resilience, and enables development for everyone.
